interpretation: Every entry is a conditional scenario family unless explicitly marked historical_reference. None is a probability-weighted forecast.

scenario_families.geography_limit: national all sectors with sector-specific renewable rows
scenario_families.use: Annual U.S. generation and renewable-capacity scenario charts through 2050.
constraints: Do not combine electric-power, end-use, and all-sector scopes.
Solar all-sector capacity mixes AC utility capacity and DC end-use capacity.
The 2025 model year is not a substitute for the EIA historical observation.

scenario_families.geography_limit: model domain excludes non-contiguous U.S. areas
scenario_families.use: Technology-rich U.S. capacity and generation comparison, including CCS, SMR, storage, distributed PV, offshore wind, and hydrogen combustion turbines.
constraints: Do not infer annual values between model years without visibly labeled interpolation.
Storage discharge and Canadian imports are not generation technologies.

scenario_families.use: Global generation and capacity pathways through 2070 and optional extension to 2100, with explicit model spread.
constraints: Never collapse model spread into a single unlabeled pathway.
Some technology variables are aggregates or overlap with component variables; choose one hierarchy level.
The Phase V physical-risk damage-function issue does not apply to this transition-electricity subset, but the release vintage must remain visible.
Respect the NGFS adapted-material redistribution restriction.

scenario_families.use: Ocean-energy capacity milestone annotation or sparse scenario line.
constraints: Do not interpolate the sparse milestone values without an explicit visual label.
Do not extend the series past 2050.
Capacity is not annual generation or economically recoverable resource.

scenario_families.use: Gold-standard interaction and causal-structure reference for the future dashboard simulator.
constraints: Public documentation supports a clean-room, architecture-compatible model, not a verified bit-for-bit clone.
Do not copy proprietary simulator code or imply MIT/Climate Interactive endorsement.
Validate future implementation against documented equations, units, reference points, and scenario behavior.

scenario_families.use: Independent long-horizon research comparison if a later dashboard view needs the full IPCC scenario ensemble.
constraints: Apply the AR6 Scenario Explorer license and vetting metadata before ingesting.

scenario_families.use: High-authority global 2050 comparison layer when licensing and automated access are resolved.
constraints: Do not redistribute the raw dataset until its current license permits the intended dashboard use.
